messages:
support-jen: Hey team, ACME tenant just reported intermittent 502s and high tail latency on their Dedicated cluster starting ~2026-03-15T18:12Z. Customer provided request_id=rcq_20260315_8f3a7 and a sample trace id trace-0x9a4c. They're asking for repro steps + logs so we can correlate traces. Can someone own collection?

jordan: I can take this. Need the tenant namespace and a curl repro we can run against the same model/route. Also want the exact pod name if available and the timespan for logs (they said start ~18:10Z).

support-jen: Namespace is dedicated-acme, route is /v1/generate (model: rwd-xl-8k). Pod reported in their UI was inference-0-6f8d7. They weren't able to run curl themselves reliably but attached a sample error response.

jordan: Cool. First: ask them to run this curl from a host in the same region (or we run it from our debug host) to reproduce the 502 and capture request id: 

curl -v -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"rwd-xl-8k","input":"short prompt to reproduce"}' \
  --write-out '\nREQUEST_ID:%{http_code}:%{remote_ip}:%{time_total}\n' \
  -o /tmp/repro_response.json

Please paste the REQUEST_ID line and the response body. Redact any full API keys.

Also we need pod logs and node diagnostics. Steps I will run: 
1) kubectl -n dedicated-acme logs inference-0-6f8d7 --since=30m > /tmp/inference-0-6f8d7.logs 2>&1
2) kubectl -n dedicated-acme get pods -o wide > /tmp/pods.txt
3) kubectl -n dedicated-acme describe pod inference-0-6f8d7 > /tmp/pod-describe.txt

Node (ssh into node): 
4) sudo journalctl -u kubelet -S '2026-03-15 18:00:00' > /tmp/kubelet-journal.log
5) sudo dmesg -T | tail -n 200 > /tmp/dmesg-tail.log
6) sudo nvidia-smi --query-gpu=index,name,utilization.gpu,utilization.memory,memory.total,memory.used --format=csv -f /tmp/gpu-snapshot.csv
7) sudo nvidia-smi dmon -s u -d 1 -o TD > /tmp/nvidia-dmon.log --run for ~30s (captures short burst behavior)
8) sudo cat /var/log/kern.log | tail -n 200 > /tmp/kern-tail.log

Bundle and upload (preferred):
9) tar -czf /tmp/acme-debugbundle-1768412345.tgz /tmp/inference-0-6f8d7.logs /tmp/pod-describe.txt /tmp/pods.txt /tmp/kubelet-journal.log /tmp/dmesg-tail.log /tmp/gpu-snapshot.csv /tmp/nvidia-dmon.log /tmp/kern-tail.log
10) aws s3 cp /tmp/acme-debugbundle-1768412345.tgz s3://redwood-support-bundles/acme/ --acl bucket-owner-full-control && post the s3 path here (or we can create a presigned upload).

Important: DO NOT include any full Authorization headers or customer PII in the bundle. If they include request bodies with sensitive tokens, redact before upload.

maria: Add to that: please also capture the inference runtime logs for the model server: /var/log/redwood/runtime.log* and the kv-cache stats endpoint (curl localhost:9000/_cache/stats) if available. Those helped in the past to correlate cache thrash with spikes.

jordan: Good call, adding that capture. Command: 
sudo cp /var/log/redwood/runtime.log* /tmp/ && curl -sS http://localhost:9000/_cache/stats > /tmp/kv-cache-stats.json

tim: I'll run the above now on the node (ssh session up). If I hit anything weird I'll paste output. Expecting ~10–15m to collect and upload.

sre-bot: Support bundle S3 prefix created: s3://redwood-support-bundles/acme/1768412345/ (ACL: restricted). Use this pre-signed upload helper if you cannot run aws cli: 
- Go to https://internal-support-upload.redwood.example and paste upload token: UPLOAD-ACME-1768412345

jordan: Thanks. After upload, please post the full s3 path and the reproduced REQUEST_ID from the curl run. I'll correlate with our trace logs (trace-0x9a4c) and check waveform around 18:12Z.

support-jen: Customer asked whether we need core dumps. Not unless you can confirm a kernel oops. Don't include core files by default (they're large and often sensitive). If we do need them we'll request explicitly and provide a secure transfer method.

tim: Upload complete: s3://redwood-support-bundles/acme/1768412345/acme-debugbundle-1768412345.tgz. Repro curl gave REQUEST_ID: 502:10.123.45.67:2.42 and response body saved to /tmp/repro_response.json (snippet: "{\"error\":\"upstream service timeout\"}"). Posting bundle link and starting a support ticket with the trace mapping.

jordan: Received, thanks. I'll pull logs and correlate with node GPU spikes. If I need additional syscall traces I'll ask for a short eBPF capture window. For now, will run analysis and report back in this thread. :thumbsup:

maria: If you find repeated KV cache evictions around the timestamps, try a quick canary rollback to rwd-xl-8k-v2 (previous variant) and see if latency stabilizes. Document results here so SRE can rollback if needed.

jordan: Will do. Leaving note for oncall to watch the rollout channel if we attempt canary.

support-jen: Great coordination — copying customer that we have the bundle and are investigating.
